record.paper_title: Problem collection from the IML programme: Graphs, Hypergraphs, and Computing
record.context_brief: Brooks-type improper colouring for planar graphs
record.original_question: For sufficiently large k, does every planar graph G with maximum degree at most 2k+2 admit a (k,k)-colouring, meaning a partition V(G)=J∪K with maximum degrees Δ(G[J])≤k and Δ(G[K])≤k?

evidence.quote: Corréa, Havet, and Sereni [1], conjectured that for sufficiently large k (say, k > 106), every planar graph G with ∆(G) ≤ 2k + 2 has a (k, k)-coloring.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let G=(V,E) be a finite simple graph. For an induced subgraph H of G, let Δ(H) denote its maximum degree. Given nonnegative integers a and b, a (a,b)-colouring of G is a partition V(G)=J∪K of the vertex set into two (possibly empty) parts such that Δ(G[J])≤a and Δ(G[K])≤b, where G[S] denotes the subgraph of G induced by S.\n\nProve or disprove: there exists an integer k₀ such that for every integer k≥k₀, every planar graph G with maximum degree Δ(G)≤2k+2 admits a (k,k)-colouring.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (attributed to Corrêa, Havet, and Sereni) that for sufficiently large k every planar graph with maximum degree at most 2k+2 admits a (k,k)-colouring appears to remain open. Searches surface the original conjecture and related work on improper colourings of planar graphs (including Mihók's construction of planar graphs that are not (k,k)-colourable for arbitrary k when the degree bound is relaxed), but no resolution of this specific Brooks-type conjecture for the bound 2k+2 was located.

status_evidence.title: About a Brooks-type theorem for improper colouring
status_evidence.snippet: Correa, Havet, and Sereni formulated Conjecture 1: There exists an integer k₀ ≥ 3 such that for any k ≥ k₀, any planar graph [with Δ ≤ 2k+2 has a (k,k)-coloring].
status_evidence.claim: Original conjecture stated; no proof located.

status_evidence.title: Defective colouring of graphs excluding a subgraph or minor
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses (k,k)-colourings of planar and minor-closed graph classes.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent literature treats the conjecture as still open.
